quizzes.title: Getting Started Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: What is Git? Install and Setup, Your First Commit, History and Undoing Things.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between Git and GitHub?
options: Git is a website and GitHub is a program on your computer
Git is a program on your computer and GitHub is a website that hosts Git repositories
They are two names for the same tool
GitHub is an older version of Git
questions.explanation: Git is the version control tool you install. GitHub is an online service that stores Git repositories so people can share them.

questions.prompt: After these commands, which hidden folder exists inside notes?
questions.code:
mkdir notes
cd notes
git init
ls -a
questions.explanation: git init creates a hidden .git folder. It holds the whole history of the project.

questions.prompt: Which area holds changes that you marked with git add but have not committed yet?
questions.explanation: git add moves changes into the staging area, the waiting room before a commit.

questions.prompt: Complete the command to save the staged changes with a message.
questions.explanation: git commit saves everything in the staging area as a new commit.

questions.prompt: Which commit message is the best?
options: Fix crash when the todo list is empty
questions.explanation: A good message starts with a verb and says what the commit does, so you can understand it months later.

questions.prompt: What happens to the new line after these commands?
options: It is saved in a new commit
It is thrown away and the file goes back to the last commit
It moves to the staging area
It moves to a new branch
questions.explanation: git restore discards uncommitted edits in the working directory. Git cannot bring them back because they were never committed.

quizzes.title: Branching Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Branches and Merging, Merge Conflicts, .gitignore, Stash and Tags.

questions.prompt: Which command creates a new branch and moves to it?
questions.explanation: git switch -c creates the branch and switches to it in one step.

questions.prompt: main has no new commits since feature-login was created. What kind of merge is this?
questions.code:
git switch main
git merge feature-login
questions.explanation: When main has not moved, Git only slides the main pointer forward. This is a fast-forward and needs no new commit.

questions.prompt: Which line comes from the branch being merged in (feature-lahore)?
questions.code:
<<<<<<< HEAD
Hello Pakistan
=======
Hello Lahore
>>>>>>> feature-lahore
questions.explanation: The part between ======= and >>>>>>> is the incoming branch. The part after <<<<<<< HEAD is your current branch.

questions.prompt: You fixed the conflict in hello.txt. Complete the command that marks it as resolved.
questions.explanation: After editing the file and removing the markers, git add tells Git the conflict is solved. Then you commit.

questions.prompt: Which of these files will Git ignore?
questions.explanation: The pattern *.log matches every file that ends in .log, such as server.log.

options: Saves uncommitted changes aside and gives you a clean folder
Creates a new branch called stash
questions.explanation: git stash puts unfinished work in a safe place. Use git stash pop to bring it back.

quizzes.title: Collaboration Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: GitHub and Remotes, Pull Requests and Team Workflow.

questions.prompt: Which command downloads new commits from GitHub but does not change your files?
questions.explanation: git fetch only downloads. git pull is fetch plus a merge into your current branch.

questions.prompt: In this command, what is origin?
questions.code:
git remote add origin https://github.com/sara/notes.git
git push -u origin main
options: A short name for the remote URL
questions.explanation: origin is the nickname Git stores for the remote repository URL. It is only a convention, but nearly everyone uses it.

options: Copies a remote repository to your computer and sets up origin
questions.explanation: git clone downloads the whole repository with its history and connects it to the original as origin.

questions.prompt: Complete the command that uploads the new branch to GitHub.
questions.explanation: git push sends your commits to the remote. The -u option remembers the link for next time.

questions.prompt: You start a new feature in a team project. What is the best first step?
options: Create a new branch for the feature
questions.explanation: Each feature gets its own branch. When it is ready you open a pull request so teammates can review it.

questions.prompt: A teammate deleted .env in a later commit, but this still prints the password. Why?
questions.code:
git rm .env
git commit -m "Remove env file"
git show HEAD~1:.env
options: The deleted file comes back after every push
History keeps the old commit, so the password is still readable
git show always prints the newest file
questions.explanation: Deleting a file only adds a new commit. The old commit still holds the content, so the password must be rotated.
